correctness.rationale: The proof checks the exact strict-upper and strict-lower sets under \(\mathbb S X=X\oplus S^0\). Every old beat witness survives, so a beat reduction of \(X\) lifts to one of \(\mathbb S X\). If a core \(C\) has at least two points, no old point becomes beat and the two new maxima are not down beat because a nontrivial minimal finite poset cannot have a greatest element. If \(|C|=1\), the three-point suspension dismantles to a point. Iteration then gives the cardinality formula. The packaged verifier exhaustively checks every labeled poset through five points, \(14864\) lifted beat deletions, and \(17892\) minimality/core-cardinality instances through three iterates. Finite enumeration is explicitly not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the general strong-homotopy core behavior of non-Hausdorff suspension, including the exact minimality criterion and iterated core-size formula. The closest inspected primary source places the core and suspension constructions side by side and uses iterated suspension for sphere models, but does not state this general interaction. A broader Alexandroff-core paper likewise does not treat suspension. Targeted database and web searches under the natural aliases found no equivalent or stronger statement. This is not treated as a proof of novelty; the conclusion rests on statement-level comparison with the most relevant accessible full texts, with the unavailable original Stong full text retained as a residual risk.
residual_risks: The original Stong article was not available in directly inspectable full text from the sources used for this review. An equivalent formulation hidden there or in an obscure older source therefore cannot be ruled out absolutely.
Search coverage is strongest for the terminology “core”, “beat point”, “minimal finite space”, and “non-Hausdorff suspension”; a historically different terminology could evade keyword search.

value.rationale: The non-Hausdorff suspension is a standard construction for finite models, while the Stong core is the canonical invariant of ordinary finite-space homotopy type. Their exact interaction is mathematically natural: the theorem gives an immediate minimality test, an explicit core without rerunning a dismantling process, and a closed formula for every suspension iterate. The result is not a parameter tweak or a finite census; it is a reusable structural lemma that separates the contractible and noncontractible cases and controls strong-homotopy complexity under a classical model-building operation.
